To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the probability of a CS delivery taking place is higher if the mother has a PHI subscription, and (ii) gynaecologists' demand for leisure affects the probability of a mother undertaking a CS delivery.
the probability of a woman having a caesarea section (CS) is positively related to the presence of a private health insurance (P.H.I) subscription.
there is patient selection in the demand for PHI and that the obstetricians’ decision to undertake CS deliveries is influenced by the women having PHI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of PHI and obstetricians' preferences on CS delivery.
a specific aspect of patient selection and gynaecologist’s demand for leisure in the demand for CS in Greece.
the influence of PHI and gynaecologist's ‘demand for leisure’ on the decision to undertake a CS delivery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the demand for private obstetric services is not independent of gynaecologist's preferences for leisure.
the private sector is not a ‘market’ for maternity services, but a ‘market’ where demand is determined by the supply of services.
the decision to undergo CS is not only influenced by the mother's characteristics but also by the obstetrician.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PHI coverage is a significant factor in explaining the demand for CS and that gynaecologists are not indifferent to the time of the week and time of the day when a CS is undertaken.
PHI coverage and obstetricians’ ‘demand for work–leisure’ are the two most important determinants of a CS delivery in private hospitals.
PHI is a ‘good’ for both the obstetrician and the mother, but the ‘price’ paid by mothers is higher than that paid by the gynaecologists, as they do not pay the full cost of the CS delivery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PHI coverage and obstetricians’ leisure demand are important determinants of the demand for private obstetric care.
the demand for PHI in maternity care is not independent from the demand for a CS.
PHI may be used by obstetricians as a means to increase their incomes.
